findings.description: `safe_git status` takes git's optional `index.lock` and holds it while it collects the status. The deadline's `kill -9` cannot be caught, so git never deletes the lock. After that, the session's `git add`, `commit`, `checkout` and `merge`, and pup's own index writes in that worktree, fail until someone removes it.
findings.body:
**A deadline kill of `git status` leaves a stale `index.lock` behind**

Every `safe_git` call now runs under `bounded`, and the watcher `kill -9`s the job at the deadline:

```sh
safe_git() {
  bounded env GIT_DIR="$GIT_ADMIN" GIT_COMMON_DIR="$GIT_COMMON" GIT_WORK_TREE="$WORKTREE" \
    git ${GIT_SAFE_CONFIG...} "$@"
}
```

The re-check runs `safe_git -C "$WORKTREE" status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all …` twice per call (lines 766-774). Nothing in the hook's environment turns off git's optional locks. The repo has no `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS` or `--no-optional-locks` anywhere, and neither `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` nor `WINDOW_GIT_CONFIG` sets them.

`cmd_status` refreshes the index, then takes `$GIT_DIR/index.lock` (`repo_hold_locked_index`) before `wt_status_collect`. It only writes or rolls the lock back after the collect finishes. So the lock is held through the slow part: the untracked walk under `--untracked-files=all`. SIGKILL skips git's tempfile cleanup, so the lock stays.

Two ways to reach it:
- **No adversary needed:** a large repo or a loaded machine (ADR 0124 measures at load average ~100) can push a plain `status` past a deadline that falls 2-4 s after the hook starts.
- **On purpose:** a fifo planted as a subdirectory `.gitignore` blocks the untracked walk while the lock is held, so the kill leaves the lock every time.

What follows: `<common>/worktrees/<id>/index.lock` stays. Every later index write in the worktree fails with `index.lock: File exists`. Later hook `status` runs just skip the optional lock, so nothing points at the cause. ADR 0124's ceiling ("not what a killed git had already done") doesn't name this effect. Before this PR nothing SIGKILLed git.

The hooks only read, so they never need the optional lock. `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` (git ≥ 2.15) also covers the short index refresh at the end of `git diff <MERGED>` (line 782).

findings.description: The re-check's 200-path cap (`RECHECK_MAX_DIRTY_PATHS`) was sized against the 5 s timeout. The loop now has a 2-4 s deadline, and each out-of-scope regular file adds a `date` plus two `bounded` calls (~5 ms each by ADR 0124's figure). So ~100-200 small out-of-scope dirty files that used to pass can now hit "ran out of time" on every call. The `3)` message would then blame a fifo or large files. Lower the cap, or measure near it and record the result.

`bounded`'s BLOCKED message always blames "a fifo where git or the hook expects a file", but it also fires when slow reads (e.g. hashing many dirty files) already spent the deadline; "…outran the hook deadline." alone, or "(a fifo, or too slow a read)", would be accurate.

The late-start deadline test has thin margins and needs `python3`. It allows ~0.4 s against `HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS*1000 - 500`, and the decoy `wc` returns 0.3 s before a 3 s watcher's kill. Under load it can refuse early as out of time and still pass without exercising the late-start path it is named for. A fake `date` that advances per call would remove both problems.

Four new tests each hand-build the same PATH shim: `mkdir bin`, look up the real tool via `command -v`, write a `for arg; do last=$arg; done … exec <real> "$@"` script, and prefix PATH. This is the third-plus use, so a `shimTool(name, bodyForPath)` helper is now warranted.

The conductor graph test sets up its repo with an inline `for (const args of [...])` git loop, a fourth repo-setup idiom in a file that already has `git(cwd, ...args)` helpers (lines 1070, 2147, 2358). Reuse one of those helpers.

The new call-site comment "Its git is pinned to the checkout's admin dir, which `refreshConductorCheckout` verifies" restates the `servedGraphConfig` JSDoc ("the dirs the launch's check verified before it handed the file over"). general.md §Comments says to delete the call-site copy.
Subject-verb slip in the Tests paragraph: "and the re-check after a call refuse with the deadline line" should read "refuses".
`bounded` treats any exit status of 137 as a deadline kill, so a command that exits 137 by itself would be reported as BLOCKED/124. This is unreachable for the `git`, `head` and `wc` it runs today.
